_readme: Single control file for the MSP AI Kit. Edit values here, then run: node .claude/skills/msp-ai-kit/scripts/build.mjs. Keys starting with an underscore are comments and are ignored. Nothing in this file is secret; never put API keys or credentials here.

company.name: Digerati Experts
company.area_served: Arizona and Greater Phoenix (Chandler, Phoenix, Scottsdale, Tempe, Mesa, Gilbert)
company.clients: small and mid-sized businesses, professional services, healthcare, and organizations with compliance or cyber-insurance pressure
company.packaging: ProActive Ecosystem packages in Office, Business, and Enterprise tiers across Core IT, Security Operations, and Backup & Disaster Recovery
company.pricing_rule: Never quote package prices, discounts, or SLAs from memory; the canonical floors live in the website pricing source and the Intelligence Hub.

tone: plain English before jargon, translating technical findings into business risk
dry confidence, with any joke landing on the problem or the attackers, never on the client
brief by default, matching the reader's register
avoid: "in today's digital landscape" and other filler

team.business_hours: Monday to Friday, 8:00 to 17:00 America/Phoenix (Arizona does not observe daylight saving time)
team.after_hours: P1 only; on-call engineer via the emergency line, everything else next business day

stack.documentation: Zoho WorkDrive and the Intelligence Hub
stack.rmm: RMM (set stack.rmm to your RMM product)
stack.backup: Backup / BCDR (set stack.backup to your backup product)
stack.email_security: Email security (set stack.email_security to your product)

sla._note: Defaults for internal triage. Set confirmed to true once Joe has approved these numbers; until then generated text labels them as working defaults and never publishes them client-facing.

priorities.name: Critical
priorities.definition: Business-wide outage, active security incident, data loss in progress, or a regulatory deadline at risk today.
priorities.examples: ransomware indicators, site down, mail flow stopped for everyone, compromised admin account

priorities.name: High
priorities.definition: A department or critical role cannot work, or a single-user issue with no workaround for a revenue-critical task.
priorities.examples: line-of-business app down for a team, executive locked out, backup job failing for 24 hours

priorities.name: Normal
priorities.definition: One user impaired with a workaround, or a non-urgent fault.
priorities.examples: printer issue, slow laptop, MFA re-enrollment, shared mailbox permission

priorities.name: Low / Request
priorities.definition: Service requests, how-to questions, scheduled changes, and improvements.
priorities.examples: new user onboarding, software install, license change, report request

escalation.when: no progress after 30 minutes on P1/P2 or 2 hours on P3, or the fix needs admin rights beyond the desk
root cause is infrastructure, identity, or vendor-level; any change that touches production servers or network core
any indicator of compromise, phishing with credential entry, malware alert, impossible-travel sign-in, or client reports a breach
client is unhappy, scope is disputed, a quote is needed, or the issue will affect a contract or renewal
P1 past 2 hours, legal or insurance notification questions, media or law-enforcement contact, or any decision that commits DE money or liability

scripting.bash: bash 5 (POSIX sh when the target may be busybox or macOS /bin/sh)
scripting.deployment: pushed through the RMM as SYSTEM or root, non-interactive, one script per task
scripting.logging: write a timestamped log under ProgramData\DE\logs (Windows) or /var/log/de/ (Linux and macOS) and echo a one-line summary for the RMM output

modules._note: true = include, false = leave out. Order and budget priority come from each module's frontmatter, not from this list.

targets._note: true = generate this output. Budgets are the hard character limits of the destination; the builder trims by module priority and reports what it dropped.
